title: Dinesh Chandra v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Disposed; theft recovery withdrawn, fresh order after hearing.
headnote: Writ against demand notices for recovery of electricity-theft dues was disposed of after the licensee withdrew the recovery. The department was left at liberty to pass a fresh order only after hearing the consumer and following the procedure under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005.
facts: Dinesh Chandra challenged three demand notices, dated 11 December 2019, 9 January 2020 and 11 January 2023, by which the electricity department sought to recover dues in a case of theft of electricity. In the writ before the Allahabad High Court, counsel for the department stated that the impugned recovery had been withdrawn and that a fresh order would be passed after the petitioner was given an opportunity of hearing.

holding_units.holding: Where the licensee withdraws demand notices for recovery of dues in a theft case, the writ is disposed of with liberty to pass a fresh order only after the consumer is heard and the procedure prescribed under the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 is followed.

principle_tags.application: The Court did not try the theft demand. It recorded the licensee's withdrawal and confined any fresh order to a hearing and the procedure under the Supply Code.

not_decided.point: Legality and quantum of any fresh theft-recovery demand
not_decided.note: The impugned recovery was withdrawn. The Court did not examine the merits and left a fresh order to the licensee after hearing.
